userPrompt: What are the penalties for a serious GDPR breach?
responseText:
**Penalties for serious GDPR breaches (as of 2025)** The **maximum administrative fines** under the EU GDPR are set out in Article 83 and are among the highest of any data protection law: ### Two-tier fine structure | Tier | Infringement | **Maximum Fine** | |------|--------------|------------------| | **Lower tier** (Art. 83(4)) | Failures in obligations of controllers/processors such as: technical & organisational measures, records of processing, data breach notification, DPIA, appointment of DPO, etc. | **€10 million or 2% of global annual turnover** (whichever is higher) | | **Higher tier** (Art. 83(5)–(6)) | **Serious breaches**, including:
• Violation of basic processing principles (Art. 5, 6, 7, 9)
• Violation of data subject rights (Arts. 12–22)
• International data transfers (Chapter V)
• Non-compliance with an order or limitation by a supervisory authority | **€20 million or 4% of global annual turnover** (whichever is higher) | ### What counts as a “serious” GDPR breach? Serious breaches that routinely attract the **4% / €20m** cap include: - Unlawful processing without a valid legal basis (especially sensitive data) - Large-scale data breaches caused by inadequate security - Ignoring data subject rights (e.g., repeated failure to honour erasure or access requests) - Unlawful international transfers (e.g., missing SCCs, no transfer impact assessment) - Processing children’s data without proper consent mechanisms - Ignoring a binding order from a Data Protection Authority (DPA) ### Additional consequences (beyond fines) - **Civil claims** for damages by affected individuals (Art. 82) — increasingly common in collective actions. - **Reputational damage** and mandatory public disclosure of the fine. - **Criminal penalties** in some Member States (e.g., up to 5 years imprisonment or unlimited fines in the UK under the DPA 2018 for the most egregious cases). - **Regulatory bans** or orders to stop processing. ### Real-world examples (serious breaches) - **Meta (Facebook)**: €1.2 billion fine (2023) for unlawful EU–US data transfers. - **Amazon Europe**: €746 million proposed (2021, later withdrawn after appeal). - **Google (CNIL)**: €50 million (2019) for transparency and consent violations. - Multiple €100m–€500m+ fines against telecoms, retailers, and public bodies for large-scale breaches. **Note**: Supervisory authorities must apply the fine that is “effective, proportionate and dissuasive” (Art. 83(1)). They consider 11 aggravating and mitigating factors (Art. 83(2)), so many serious breaches still receive fines well below the legal maximum. For the most current guidance, refer to the **European Data Protection Board (EDPB) Guidelines 04/2022 on the calculation of administrative fines** and the fining practices published by your national DPA.
